clue.text: Flower always preserved?

annotationWithheld.why: Flower always preserved? (6): EVER (always) in SN (tin), with 'preserved' giving both the tin and the containment, one word doing two jobs

clue.text: A number supporting feature as tree

indicators.note: in a down clue a piece that supports another sits beneath it

parts.note: the chin is a feature of the face
qua is Latin for 'in the capacity of', i.e. as
a PIN is a personal identification number

explanation.surface: A numeral holds up some feature that works as a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporting' puts PIN below CHIN QUA in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The chinquapin is a North American chestnut species, a small tree or shrub.

clue.text: Notice dirt raked up under study — that's extra

indicators.note: in a down clue the next piece sits under the one before it

parts.note: an ad is a notice, an advertisement
a den is a private study room

indicators.note: raked up in a down entry means the word for dirt is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: mud is dirt

explanation.surface: Someone spots raked-up dirt beneath their study, an unwelcome bonus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raked up' reverses the dirt word in this down entry, and 'under' sets it below the study; 'Notice' looks like a verb but is the noun for an advert.
explanation.definitionFit: An addendum is an addition, something extra appended to a text.

clue.text: Watch teacher marking bright student?

definitions.meaning: slang for a watch, from its ticking
a bright student's work gets ticks, so the teacher marking it is one who ticks

explanation.definitionFit: A watch is informally called a ticker, and one who ticks work is literally a ticker.

clue.text: Moreover, iron bar's put up as aid to locomotion and respiration

indicators.note: put up in a down entry means the whole string of pieces is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: too means moreover, also
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
but means bar, except

explanation.surface: An iron bar is erected to help with moving and breathing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' reverses TOO FE BUT as one run, giving TUBEFOOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Starfish and sea urchins use tube feet both to move about and to take in oxygen.

clue.text: Releasing new comedy film series following win

indicators.note: releasing means letting go of the letter that stands for new

parts.note: the Carry On films are a long-running series of British comedy films
ff is the abbreviation for 'and following (pages)'

explanation.surface: A new comedy film series is launched after a victory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Releasing' drops the letter for new from the film series name. Carry On films are bawdy British comedies of the 1950s to 1970s; the definition is just 'win'.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry off a prize is to win it.

clue.text: Curdling blood fee, refreshment better at 18

indicators.note: curdling means turning these words thick and lumpy, a breaking up of their letters

explanation.surface: A bloodcurdling tale of a fee, a drink and a gamble at a numbered place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curdling' rearranges BLOOD FEE REFRESHMENT BETTER AT; 'curdling blood' also fits the horror theme. The definition is 18-across, the murderer Sweeney Todd.
explanation.definitionFit: The Demon Barber of Fleet Street is the familiar epithet of the fictional murderer Sweeney Todd.

clue.text: 18's speciality is pâté, mixed under supervision of author

indicators.note: in a down entry the mixed letters sit beneath the author, as if supervised from above

parts.note: the setter, as author, refers to himself as me

indicators.note: mixed means the letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A villain's signature dish of pâté is blended under the author's eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' rearranges the six letters of 'is pâté', and 'under supervision of' sets them below the setter's self-reference. Sweeney Todd's accomplice baked his victims into pies.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Sweeney Todd story, meat pies made from the victims are Mrs Lovett's notorious speciality.

clue.text: Pardon me for spreading rumour that VIP's my mate

indicators.note: spreading means the letters are scattered and laid out afresh

explanation.surface: An apology from someone gossiping that a celebrity is their friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spreading' rearranges PARDON ME. 'Pardon me for' reads as an apology, but these are the fodder and a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Name-dropping is casually mentioning famous acquaintances to impress, as in claiming a VIP as a friend.

clue.text: See 6
Give insufficient resources to combat style of bowling

definitions.meaning: to supply too few weapons for fighting
delivery with the hand below shoulder level, as in cricket or rounders

explanation.definitionFit: Under-arm means to provide too few arms, and underarm is a low-handed throwing action.

clue.text: Officers served up squidgy flan in mess

indicators.note: served up suggests food dished out anyhow, so the letters come out in a new order
in a mess means the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Squishy flan dished up in the officers' mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' and 'in mess' both signal an anagram of SQUIDGY FLAN. The Flying Squad is a Metropolitan Police unit in London.
explanation.definitionFit: The Flying Squad is a team of police officers dealing with armed robbery.

clue.text: Hustler going out with painter

indicators.note: going out suggests the word for a hustler leaving its form, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: and means with, together

explanation.surface: A conman is dating an artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Graham Sutherland was a twentieth-century English artist, known for portraits and landscapes.

clue.text: Oxygen gas — a problem for the goalkeeper?

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen
neon is a noble gas
a means one

explanation.surface: Gases that trouble a goalie, oddly.
explanation.walkthrough: A striker one-on-one with the goalkeeper has only the keeper to beat.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-on-one, a striker alone against the keeper, is a goalkeeper's worst situation.

clue.text: In a small court what they used to charge for a TV series

indicators.note: in means the earlier charge is placed inside the court abbreviation

parts.note: CT is the abbreviation for court
an old fee is the price they once charged

explanation.surface: In a minor court, a former fee is quoted for a television programme.
explanation.walkthrough: Cold Feet is a British TV comedy-drama.
explanation.definitionFit: Cold Feet is a British television comedy-drama series first shown in 1997.

clue.text: See 6
The City's still happy

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London
static means still, motionless

explanation.surface: The City financial district remains cheerful.
explanation.walkthrough: EC is the postal district of the City of London, the financial centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecstatic means overjoyed, very happy indeed.

clue.text: Revs will pepper

parts.note: reverends are good men, PI (pious) MEN
in headline style 'to' marks the future, as in 'Bishops to visit', so it stands for will

explanation.surface: Engines turning over will spice things up.
explanation.walkthrough: Revs is short for reverends, not engine turns. Pimento is a sweet red pepper.
explanation.definitionFit: Pimento is a sweet red pepper, the kind stuffed into olives.

clue.text: Having taken a lot of demerara rum, marshal admitted murderer

indicators.note: admitted means let inside, taking the marshal in

parts.words: Having taken a lot of demerara
parts.note: someone who has taken plenty of demerara sugar is sweet
Michel Ney was one of Napoleon's marshals
rum means odd, strange

explanation.surface: A marshal confesses to murder after heavy sugar and rum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitted' sets Napoleon's marshal inside the sugary word; rum here means strange, not the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweeney Todd is the fictional barber who murders his customers.

clue.text: Insubstantial point spanning the years

indicators.note: spanning places the compass point within the two year abbreviations

parts.note: Y is the abbreviation for year, doubled for the plural
east is a compass point

explanation.surface: A trivial point stretching across the years.
explanation.walkthrough: YY for years follows the convention of doubling a letter for a plural, as in pp.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeasty means frothy, light and lacking substance.

clue.text: See 8
See 7
Rabelais novel that may be exalted

indicators.note: novel means new, so the author's name is given a new order

explanation.definitionFit: Something raisable can be raised, lifted up or elevated.

clue.text: Squeeze mineral in abundance

parts.note: a squeeze is slang for a girlfriend, a gal
ore is mineral-bearing rock

explanation.walkthrough: Squeeze is slang for a partner, not a press.
explanation.definitionFit: Galore means in plenty, in large numbers.

clue.text: Desires stepchildren to cuff one

indicators.note: to cuff means to enclose like a handcuff around a wrist

parts.note: read as step-children: PAS, a dance step, followed by SONS, children
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Stepchildren are wanting to hit somebody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stepchildren' splits into step (PAS) and children (SONS); 'to cuff' puts I inside, after PASS.
explanation.definitionFit: Passions are strong desires or enthusiasms.
